A huge turbine that grows with its size. Count its sections: width × height ÷ 9 × length (a 3×3×3 is 3, a 7×9×15 is 105). It takes up to 40 mB/t of steam per section, at {fe:20}, {fe:36} or {fe:56} FE per mB of Steam, High-Pressure or Superheated Steam. A 7×9×15 on Superheated Steam makes {fe:235200} FE/t before its bonuses.
Its output cap is a full flow of Superheated Steam with both bonuses, and it holds 400 ticks of that; its energy ports share the cap.
Its rotor spins up over a few seconds when steam flows, and the output rises with it. The better the steam, the faster it spins. The rotor fills the cross-section's shorter side.
Build a hollow tube on either horizontal axis: a cross-section 3 to 7 wide and 3 to 9 tall, 3 to 15 long. In a 3×3 tube only the corners must be casings; in a bigger one all twelve edges must be. Its front is the side with the most glass (or the side you finish it from). A new turbine starts without ports: set an energy port and a steam port with the Wrench (see Conduits & the Wrench). With an odd cross-section the middles of the ends are its generator and bearing.
Heavy Oil or Seed Oil in its lubricant tank (4,000 mB, through a lubricant port) adds 8% to its output and doubles how fast the rotor spins up, using 1 mB a second per 3 sections.
# Exhaust
Set an Exhaust port with the Wrench and spent steam leaves as Exhaust Steam instead of venting. While it drains (its exhaust tank isn't full) the turbine makes 10% more FE, on top of lubricant. With no Exhaust port it vents as before.
